clue.text: Is mum's seafood chowder out of the ordinary?

indicators.note: out of means the following letter is removed from the dish

parts.note: a chowder is a thick soup, and a seafood one could be clam soup
O is a standard abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether their mother's fish soup is anything special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is mum's' reads as a mother owning chowder; it is really 'is mum' (keeps quiet), with 's as a link. 'out of' removes O from CLAM SOUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mum means staying silent, and to clam up is the idiom for falling suddenly silent.

clue.text: Grey hollow chimney muffles roaring

indicators.note: muffles means the outer pair wraps around what follows, as a cloth muffles sound
hollow means the word chimney is emptied, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: roaring means very loud

explanation.surface: A dull chimney deadens the roar of the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' empties chimney to its two outer letters, and 'muffles' wraps them round a word for roaring; 'Grey' is the weather, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey sky is an overcast one, full of cloud, so grey and cloudy are synonyms of the weather.

clue.text: Top moral tale potentially fruitful for one growing

indicators.note: Top as a verb means cut off the head, so the first letter of the tale goes

parts.note: a parable is a short story told to teach a moral

explanation.surface: An improving story might bear fruit for a young person growing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like praise for the tale; it is a verb, beheading PARABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Land fit for ploughing and crops is potentially productive for a farmer raising them.

clue.text: Chuck rugby player's footwear

parts.note: to chuck is to throw, or sling
a back is a rugby position; the 's supplies the final S

explanation.surface: Someone throws a rugby player's boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a name; it is a verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Slingbacks are shoes held on by a strap round the heel, so they are a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Misled don

definitions.meaning: fooled or teased, as in 'you're having me on'
to don is to put clothing on

explanation.surface: A university lecturer was deceived.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has two senses: deceived as a joke, and dressed oneself in a garment.

clue.text: Mean goblin bashed elf's head

indicators.note: bashed means the word goblin is knocked out of shape
the head of the elf is its first letter

explanation.surface: A spiteful goblin hit an elf on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bashed' rearranges GOBLIN to IGNOB; 'head' adds E from elf.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of base or dishonourable is a synonym of this adjective.

clue.text: Unevenness of one motorway leads to blooming awful puncture

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: the leads of the two words are their first letters

parts.note: to lance is to pierce or puncture

explanation.surface: A wobble on the motorway leads to a dreadful puncture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' gives BA from blooming and awful; 'blooming' is British slang for 'damned'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack of balance between parts is an unevenness, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Occasion in legend regularly overlooked

indicators.note: every other letter is skipped over, keeping the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A notable event in a myth is routinely ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link: the even letters of 'in legend' are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasion means necessity or reason, as in 'there is no occasion to worry'.

clue.text: Repaired chair ably, short of arm

indicators.note: repaired means the letters are put back together in a new order
short means the word ably loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A chair fixed competently but missing an arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims ABLY to ABL; 'Repaired' rearranges CHAIR plus ABL. The definition is 'of arm', not 'arm'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to the upper limb, as in the brachial artery.

clue.text: Approved retailers getting rid of five European diamonds

indicators.note: getting rid of means the following letter is removed

parts.note: vendors are sellers
V is the Roman numeral five
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Shops dumping European diamonds was sanctioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting rid of' removes V from VENDORS.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to give backing or sanction, so the past participle means approved.

clue.text: Arab megalomaniac's not all there

indicators.note: only part of the long word is present, so the answer sits inside it

explanation.surface: A power-mad Arab is mentally unsound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all there' looks like a jibe about sanity; it signals a part of 'megalomaniac's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Oman, on the Arabian peninsula, is an Arab.

clue.text: Large antelope chasing bat over plateau

indicators.note: chasing means the following pieces come after the first
over means the word bat is turned back to front

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A big antelope pursues a bat across high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns bat round, giving TAB, and 'chasing' places the large antelope after it; 'bat' is the word itself, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableland is an elevated, flat expanse of ground, which is what a plateau is.

clue.text: Thoroughly chaotic in Lidl, get close to apoplexy

indicators.note: chaotic means the letters are jumbled
the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A shopper is driven to rage by a messy Lidl supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaotic' rearranges IN LIDL GET to DILIGENTL; 'close to' adds Y from apoplexy. Lidl is a discount supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Working diligently means working with care and persistence, so it is done in a thorough way.

clue.text: Hammer-wielder having appropriated gold from writer

indicators.note: having appropriated means something is taken away, as gold is stolen
from names the word the gold is taken out of

parts.note: a writer is an author
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone with a hammer has stolen gold from an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having appropriated ... from' takes AU out of AUTHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse god of thunder carries the hammer Mjolnir, so he is a famous wielder of one.

clue.text: Leaders in government office organised reform

indicators.note: the leaders of the two words are their first letters

parts.note: something organised has been put straight, tidy and in order

explanation.surface: Top civil servants arranged a policy overhaul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders in' gives GO; 'organised' is a synonym, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a criminal life and become honest is to reform, the idiom for which is this phrase.

clue.text: Cracking any video game in first excursion

indicators.note: cracking means breaking open, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Beating a video game on the first attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' rearranges ANY VIDEO GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's first journey after launch is its inaugural trip, the phrase used for any debut outing.

clue.text: One unwelcome in bed, periodically displaying clock

definitions.meaning: a weed is a plant nobody wants in a flower bed
the fluffy seed head of this plant is called a clock, shown at a certain stage of each year

explanation.surface: An unwanted bedfellow keeps looking at the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' and 'clock' suggest a bedroom; they are a flower bed and a seed head.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow flower is a common garden weed whose seed head children blow to tell the time.

clue.text: Chips are all over the place, but not totally global

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chips are scattered everywhere, though not across the whole world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges CHIPS ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspheric lens departs slightly from a true sphere, so it is not perfectly ball-shaped.

clue.text: Lose timid people outside climbing mountains

indicators.note: outside means the first word wraps around what follows

parts.note: mice are a figure for meek, timid people

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Alps are a European mountain range

explanation.surface: Nervous folk get lost on mountain climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads the range upwards as SPLA in this down clue, and 'outside' wraps the timid people round it; 'mice' for meek folk is a set phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in the wrong place is to mislay it, which is a way of losing it.

clue.text: Camouflaged creatures stay in groups

parts.note: to stick is to stay put
sects are religious or factional groups

explanation.surface: Animals in disguise keep together in groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a piece of the answer, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects look like twigs, hiding from predators by mimicking their surroundings.

clue.text: Welshman in Russian space station, far above ground

indicators.note: in means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station
Dai is a typical Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A Welsh astronaut aboard Mir, high above the Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; Dai is the stock Welshman's name of crosswords and jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspended in the sky, well off the ground, is in mid-air.

clue.text: Advanced hospital staff can be found here

definitions.text: hospital staff can be found here
definitions.meaning: nurses are found on a ward of a hospital

explanation.surface: Senior medical staff are found in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as ON WARD for the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means forward-moving, and split in two names where hospital nurses work.

clue.text: Have confidence, dance with energy

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Be self-assured and dance with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To trust that something good will happen is to expect it with optimism, a form of confidence.

clue.text: Information terminal in store, share age

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the terminal of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: A shop's information desk talks about sharing out by age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal in' gives E from store. GEN is British slang for facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A generation is people born at the same time, also used for a period of time like an age.

clue.text: Keen flier, not student, right?

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out

parts.note: an eagle is a bird, something that flies
L is for a learner, a student driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic pilot who is not a learner, correct?
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes L from EAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enthusiastic and impatient for something is being keen, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lark rising in the afternoon over river

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: PM, post meridiem, marks the afternoon
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A songbird climbs over a river in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses PMOR. 'Lark' is a frolic, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a spree or bit of fun, which is what a playful frolic is.

clue.text: Rogue ignores an argument

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means wayward or out of control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scoundrel brushes off a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like the subject; it rearranges IGNORES AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of logical thought put forward as a case is an argument.

clue.text: Month back, peeled oval fruit

indicators.note: back means the month is written backwards

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August

indicators.note: peeled means the outer letters are stripped off, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A month later, an oval fruit is peeled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses AUG to GUA; 'peeled' leaves VA from oval.
explanation.definitionFit: The guava is a tropical fruit with pink or white flesh.

clue.text: Discredit knight following mass in church

indicators.note: following means the next letter comes after
in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a heap is a mass or pile
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight's reputation is damaged after Mass in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests a church service but means a pile; 'in' sets it inside the Church of England, and 'following' adds the knight after.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower the worth or dignity of someone is to cheapen them, which discredits them.

clue.text: Soldiers, exhausted, went to bed

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
exhausted means worn out

explanation.surface: Worn-out troops turned in for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire for the night is a formal idiom for going off to sleep.
